author: Inside Edition
description: A pregnant woman suffered a horrific attack on the day of her due date. Two pitbulls charged at the expectant mom and her little chihuahua. The dogs latched onto her pregnant belly. Neighbors heard the woman's screams and ran to help. Renee Wilson, a mom of three, was attacked outside her apartment in Tacoma, Washington. Inside Edition spoke with Wilson from the hospital. A GoFundMe has been set up to help Wilson recover. For more information, you can click this link: https://www.gofundme.com/f/support-a-mother-injured-days-before-welcoming-her-baby
title: Pregnant Woman Attacked By 2 Pitbulls On Her Due Date

author: Inside Edition
description: Inside Edition got a taste of colonial times at the King's Arms in Williamsburg, Virginia. Some of the food that would have been served at a grand banquet in 1776 would have included a minimum of six meats. There were also dishes of stuffed pounded means that were called "olives" but did not include olives. The term referred to the shape. Multiple savory pieces would also be served. The layers of crust kept the food insulated so it could get to the table warm.
title: What Foods Would Have Been Served At A Banquet In 1776?

author: Inside Edition
description: A Georgia woman is lucky to be alive after a lightning strike sent her into cardiac arrest in a church parking lot. Mary Menna, who goes by "Jeanne," was volunteering at Saint Joseph Catholic School in Marietta, Georgia, when a storm moved in. Lightning hit a nearby tree, splitting it in half. The tree then hit her, sending her into cardiac arrest. She was taken to a hospital and amazed doctors with her recovery. Menna returned to the church parking lot where it happened Monday, to meet and hug the first responders who saved her life.
title: Woman Miraculously Survives Lightning Strike Outside Georgia Church
